column1: # THE FORMATTER (docs/design/FMT.0.md): source to its agreed form.
# Both runners assert three things per row: the text is what fmt(src)
# writes; fmt(expect) is expect again (a fixed point); and, where the
# source evaluates, the canon-hash of src and of expect agree -- the
# same document. Rows are written from the canonical port and held to
# the Go port. Escapes: \n newline, \t tab, \\ backslash.
# Mode `fmt-refuse` pins a source the formatter REFUSES: `expect` is
# the verdict and the finding codes, joined by a colon and commas.
# Nothing is written on a refusal, so the file is intact either way --
# what the row holds is that both ports refuse the same sources.

column1: # A MULTI-DOCUMENT SOURCE -- two top-level bags, which the unifier
# reads as a list of two documents -- formats to a single map, and
# the self-check catches it: `{a:1}\n{b:2}` evaluates to
# [{"a":1},{"b":2}] and the written text to {"a":1,"b":2}. Refused
# in both ports rather than written, so no file is corrupted; the
# defect is that a document the engine reads has no agreed form.
